focus_area_title: Get in the Habit of Discussing Your Team's Impact
content_text_body:
When teams remind themselves of the positive impacts of their work, they are more likely to feel like the work is meaningful. The goal here is to create a habit of discussing your team's positive impacts on each other, on the company, for your customers, and for the world.

### Reflect on your impact

Even if each team member only has a small role, your team impacts larger organizational goals. 

As a group, reflect on the big problems that your team's work helps solve. Ask the group: Who does the team's work help? What effects does the team have on co-workers? What is your team working on today that will make a positive difference for the organization or the world in the future?

### Align work to high-level goals

Next, list upcoming tasks that your team needs to accomplish. Brainstorm the bigger picture goals or outcomes to which each task will contribute. Next to each task, note how the task will contribute to positive impacts. 

For example, let's say the team is tasked with creating a Q&A page on the company's website. This task will positively impact customers by helping them quickly find the answers to their questions. It will positively affect the customer service team by reducing the amount of time spent answering the same questions. It will help the company as a whole by improving efficiency among the customer service team.

The team leader should post the list somewhere visible and organize additional discussions as new tasks and projects begin.
